text:
pagerbot: PAGING — auth-service heartbeat anomaly in us-west-2. 5x normal auth attempts, increased 502 rate at edge. Suspicious repeated header pattern. link: https://logs.redwood/o/abcd/query?id=auth-heartbeat-6161234567 :pager:

oncall-eng: Got the page, joining. Are we seeing customer-facing errors?

sre-amy: Seeing spike in 502s from auth-proxy (replica-3). Error looks like downstream timeout to token-service. No alerts from db.

infra-noah: Rolling up infra view — network egress looks normal. I see a small burst of connections coming from a narrow ASN (AS39523) hitting /v1/token repeatedly.

sec-eli: Can someone paste a sample log line? Need to check for leaked headers or API keys.

sre-amy: Pasting redacted snippet from edge logs:

```
[2026-03-17T14:02:10Z] src=198.51.100.23 x-forwarded-for="198.51.100.23" method=POST path=/v1/token status=502 resp_time=1200 user_agent="curl/7.79" auth_header="Bearer sk_live_***" trace=tx-8f3b
```

sec-eli: That auth_header looks like a live token pattern. If real tokens are in logs, treat this as potential exposure. Start key rotation and token invalidation plan.

oncall-eng: Confirming customer impact: metrics show a 2% increase in failed token exchanges for hosted API keys; few customer support tickets about auth errors. Low severity for most customers but could worsen.

customer-success-jordan: I’m triaging incoming tickets — two enterprise customers reported intermittent auth failures since 14:00 UTC. No confirmed data breach from customers yet. Keep me posted for messaging.

infra-noah: I can remove the edge log forwarding rule for the affected pool immediately to stop further sink exposure. Will do that now and confirm.

infra-noah: Done — edge-forwarder for pool-auth-west disabled.

sre-amy: Re-running log query to see if new requests still include auth headers in logs. Query: `level:info AND path:/v1/token AND auth_header:*` — previous pattern shows tokens recorded in header field.

pagerbot: Deploy bot: rolling restart of auth-proxy replicas scheduled as a containment step. Deploy ID: d-98f.

oncall-eng: Sec/Eli, what scope for rotation? Do we rotate all API keys in the pool or only affected tokens?

sec-eli: Immediate actions: 1) Revoke the leaked token class (if we can identify prefix). 2) Rotate service account keys used by edge-forwarder. 3) Initiate customer key rotation guidance for enterprise customers. We should not mass-rotate all customer API keys yet — target affected credentials first.

legal-kate: If user credentials were logged and forwarded, we need to prepare a legal checklist. Please tag me when we have confirmed scope and affected accounts.

sre-amy: I’m capturing the list of token prefixes seen in logs and matching them against active tokens. Running `SELECT token_id FROM tokens WHERE token_prefix IN (...)` from ops read replica.

sec-eli: Also enabling additional audit-level logging on token service to track any suspicious usage of potentially leaked tokens.

customer-success-jordan: For the two enterprise customers, can we proactively rotate their service tokens and offer a one-time migration helper? They asked to be notified via their SLA channel.

infra-noah: Confirmed no new header lines recorded since disabling forwarder. Burst stopped ~14:05 UTC.

oncall-eng: Auth-proxy restart completed. 502s dropped back to baseline.

sre-amy: Matched three token prefixes from logs to active tokens: tok_ab12, tok_ab13, tok_zz99. tok_zz99 is internal staging-only; tok_ab12 and tok_ab13 map to customer accounts C-501 and C-502.

sec-eli: Action: Revoke tok_ab12 and tok_ab13, create replacement tokens, notify CS to coordinate rotation. Also rotate the edge-forwarder credentials and any S3 log sink credentials.

customer-success-jordan: Acknowledged — will open tickets with C-501 and C-502, advise immediate rotation and provide migration steps.

legal-kate: Please save all original logs in WORM storage and mark for chain-of-custody. We might need timelines for notification obligations.

nontechnical-note: (internal) minimal customer impact observed; two customers require forced rotation.

sre-amy: Revocation commands executed: `POST /admin/tokens/revoke {token_prefix: "tok_ab12"}` and `POST /admin/tokens/revoke {token_prefix: "tok_ab13"}` — responses success. New tokens issued and handed to CS via secure channel.

sec-eli: Rotated edge-forwarder service keys in KMS and updated deployments. Also rotated S3 sink creds and reconfigured forwarder to redact headers at source.

pagerbot: Incident update: containment achieved, forwarding disabled, affected tokens revoked, service restarted. Severity: P2 -> monitoring.

oncall-eng: Recommended follow-ups: 1) Post-incident runbook update to prevent logging of Authorization headers at edge; 2) Add automated scrubber prior to any log sink; 3) Postmortem within 72 hours.

legal-kate: Noted. I’ll coordinate notification timing with CS once we have final scope.

sec-eli: I’ll prepare an incident summary with indicators-of-compromise and remediation steps.

customer-success-jordan: I’ll send templated notice to impacted contacts and keep support bridge open.

oncall-eng: Handoff to daytime SRE rotation — @sre-amy will continue to own monitoring, @infra-noah will own key rotations, @sec-eli will own communications for security.

sre-amy: Taking over monitoring.

infra-noah: Standing by on rotations.

sec-eli: I’ll update the incident channel with the final summary when ready.

pagerbot: Incident closed to active pager at 2026-03-17T14:11:30Z. Please file postmortem and runbook updates. :white_check_mark:
